records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:157 — Calendar updates use the caller’s credentials instead of the booking organizer’s, preventing reliable updates when an attendee adds guests.
records.rationale: The handler explicitly permits non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` check at the FORBIDDEN gate), but then builds the EventManager with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` — the caller's credentials — rather than the booking organizer's (`booking.user` was fetched with credentials included, suggesting that was intended). An attendee adding guests would use their own (likely nonexistent) calendar credentials, so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` would fail or no-op. Mechanism fully visible in the diff.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:91 — Attendees are persisted before the calendar update, so update failures leave guests saved and notifications unsent while retries reject those guests as existing attendees, with no recoverable synchronization mechanism.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: addGuests.handler.ts persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany BEFORE calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) and the try/catch sendAddGuestsEmails. If updateCalendarAttendees throws, guests are already saved but calendar/emails never sent. On retry, uniqueGuests filters out `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and throws BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' when the list is empty, so retries of the original request are permanently rejected — a real, verifiable consist
